fields.role: An uncanny toad that approaches the party, looks at them quizzically, and speaks the single croaking word 'Betrayal'.
fields.title: Huge Warty Toad

fields.role: Sir Chyde's brother, said by inherited documents to be buried beside him and to be a distant ancestor of the inheriting PC.
fields.title: Brigford the Wise

fields.role: A fairy giant slain by Sir Chyde with the sword later buried among his notable grave goods.
fields.title: Butter-for-Bones

fields.role: The fairy lord who ruled Dolmenwood before mortals arrived, holding it in eternal winter through armies of frost elves. Mortals defeated and exiled him to Fairy about nine centuries ago, but fear of his return persists.
fields.title: The Cold Prince

fields.role: A feared cult of sorcerers who covet and jealously guard Dolmenwood's stone circles and ley lines. Common folk associate them with occult machinations, kidnappings, and rumored human sacrifice and are afraid even to speak their name.
fields.title: The Drune

fields.role: The collective races native to the undying realm of Fairy. Most never cross into the mortal world; those encountered in Dolmenwood are often romantics, obsessives, megalomaniacs, or outcasts who entered or remained there.
fields.title: Fairies

fields.role: The Cold Prince's immortal fairy people, described as fair as snow and cruel as ice; they formed part of his forces in the war for Dolmenwood.
fields.title: Frost Elves

fields.role: A supernatural owl apparition that watches from a high branch and can cause a witnessing PC to faint unless they save versus spells.
fields.title: Ghostly Violet-Eyed Owl

fields.role: A group of 1d4 lantern-bearing goblin merchants who cautiously emerge from a trapdoor after crossing from Fairy to Dolmenwood in search of rare night-fruits.
fields.title: Tipsy Goblin Merchants

fields.role: The mysterious sorcerous maiden whom common folklore names as Sir Chyde's beloved; deeper research identifies her as the fairy princess Snowfall-at-Dusk.
fields.title: The Lady of the Wood

fields.role: A near-mythical mortal knight and hero of the war against the Cold Prince. He loved Princess Snowfall-at-Dusk, died in the final battle on the High Wold, and lingers as a phantom because of their soul-binding ring.
fields.title: Sir Chyde

fields.role: The seventeenth daughter of the Cold Prince and Sir Chyde's fairy beloved. Her father imprisoned her in Fairy; she later contacts mortals through dreams and waits to recover Sir Chyde's ring and complete their wedding.
fields.title: Princess Snowfall-at-Dusk

fields.role: Sir Chyde's patron saint and the patron saint of crusaders and knife-makers.
fields.title: St Sedge

fields.role: The resident priest who maintained the tomb and chapel as a pilgrimage site; disturbing dreams and visitations led the priest to recommend abandonment.
fields.title: Priest Attendant of Sir Chyde's Tomb

fields.role: An unnamed wizard who gives the party a map to an old Dolmenwood burial mound and pays them to recover Sir Chyde's ring.
fields.title: Wizard Patron

fields.text: Death does not end the ring's bond. Sir Chyde's spirit is called back to linger as a phantom in his tomb; the princess's prison in Fairy and the tomb in the mortal world are slowly drawn together until the two realms nearly touch; and the princess and knight can communicate verbally while dreaming of reunion and marriage.
fields.title: Effects of the Ring of Soul-Binding

fields.text: A portrait of Princess Snowfall-at-Dusk commissioned by Sir Chyde and placed among his grave goods.
fields.title: The Lady of the Wood

fields.text: A magical fairy engagement ring bestowed by Snowfall-at-Dusk on Sir Chyde: a bronze band set with a moonstone, with fittings shaped like woven branches. It binds their souls together for eternity, allows communion across imprisonment and death, and binds Sir Chyde's ghost to it. The full item is referenced on page 24 of the source adventure.
fields.title: Ring of Soul-Binding

fields.text: Winter's Daughter is a short Dolmenwood adventure about the forbidden love between the mortal knight Sir Chyde and a fairy princess during the ancient war between mortals and fairies. Sir Chyde's sealed tomb has remained closed for centuries and contains secrets and treasure.
fields.title: Adventure Premise

fields.text: The tomb has rested quietly. Snowfall-at-Dusk remains imprisoned and forgotten by her father, patiently seeking reunion with Sir Chyde. The Drune now frequent the Whything Stones.
fields.title: Centuries After the Tomb Was Sealed

fields.text: The common tale says Sir Chyde fell in love during the war with the Lady of the Wood, a sorcerous maiden of mysterious origin. They met deep in Dolmenwood and pledged their hearts by exchanging engagement rings.
fields.title: Common Folklore: Sir Chyde and the Lady

fields.text: Common folk know that Sir Chyde died in the final battle on the High Wold and asked to be buried deep in the forest. The Lady was never seen again; some say she died in the glade where the pair first met.
fields.title: Common Folklore: Sir Chyde's Death and the Lady's Fate

fields.text: Common folk say the Cold Prince ruled Dolmenwood before mortals, covering it in eternal frost and snow. About 900 years ago, mortals fought his fairy armies for control of the forest and ultimately exiled him to Fairy. They fear that the banishment weakens in winter and that he still seeks to reclaim his kingdom.
fields.title: Common Folklore: The Cold Prince

fields.text: Woldish is the common tongue. Old Woldish is an ancient dialect largely incomprehensible to Woldish speakers. Drunic is the Drune's secret language. Liturgic is sacred to the Church of the One True God. Sylvan is common among fairies and fairy-kin, though mortal speakers invariably sound foolish. High Elfish is the language of fairy nobility and is utterly unfathomable to mortals. The Immortal Tongue of Fairy is an ancient, reality-bending language known only to the oldest and most dreadful fairies.
fields.title: Languages Used in Dolmenwood

fields.text: Princess Snowfall-at-Dusk has found a way to contact the mortal world through dreams. Her professed love for the PC is a deception intended to make the infatuated adventurer recover Sir Chyde's ring for her.
fields.title: Truth Behind the Lady's Dreams

fields.text: Sir Chyde was buried with the sword he used to slay the fairy giant Butter-for-Bones, his moonstone engagement ring, and the commissioned portrait of the Lady.
fields.title: Research Fact: Notable Grave Goods

fields.text: Sir Chyde's betrothed was a fairy princess, making their relationship a forbidden love.
fields.title: Research Fact: Identity of the Lady of the Wood

fields.text: The ring Sir Chyde wore was a magic item from Fairy that bound his soul to the Lady's.
fields.title: Research Fact: Sir Chyde's Ring

fields.text: Sir Chyde's tomb remained a pilgrimage site for years until a series of hauntings led the Church to install magical wards and seal it.
fields.title: Research Fact: Why the Tomb Was Sealed

fields.text: The ring carries a fairy enchantment: Sir Chyde's ghost is bound to it and will haunt anyone who steals it. The source points to the Epilogue on page 23 for the consequence.
fields.title: Complication of Stealing the Ring

fields.text: Dolmenwood occupies a mortal region where Fairy is close enough that its inhabitants may be heard but normally cannot be touched or reached by mortals. Only certain places or times overlap, allowing passage between realms; the adventure contains one such place. Calling Fairy 'Elfland' is imprecise because elves are not its only inhabitants.
fields.title: The Mortal World and Fairy

fields.text: The stone circle's eldritch runes reflect moonlight. If deciphered, the magical script appears to serve some role in summoning rituals. Clearing moss from the bases reveals carved icy fey figures wailing and writhing as though tormented.
fields.title: Runes and Hidden Carvings at the Whything Stones

fields.description: The approach passes through tangled forest with brambles half-burying the paths and twisted trees that seem to close behind the PCs. Ahead stands an evidently artificial, flat-topped hillock; irregular clanking metal can be heard from area 2.
fields.title: Approaching the Burial Mound

fields.description: A chapel dedicated to Sir Chyde's patron saint, built into his tomb.
fields.title: Chapel of St Sedge

fields.description: A weird fairy-tale forest in the mortal world where Fairy lies unusually close. The adventure may be placed in any Dolmenwood hex outside the Witching Ring, Chell, because its events are not tied to a specific forest location.
fields.title: Dolmenwood

fields.description: A magical doorway on the lower level of Sir Chyde's tomb that leads to Snowfall-at-Dusk's realm in Fairy. The Lady claims that a bearer of Sir Chyde's ring can pass through it.
fields.title: Lower-Level Door to Fairy

fields.description: The immortal realm adjoining the mortal world near Dolmenwood, also sometimes called Elfland. It is endless and timeless, inhabited by elves and many other fairy beings, generally intangible to mortals except at special places or times where the realms overlap and permit transit.
fields.title: Fairy

fields.description: The hills where Sir Chyde was slain in the final battle between mortal and fairy forces.
fields.title: The High Wold

fields.description: Thirteen rusty iron owls hang with spread wings from trees around the Whything Stones, clanking in the breeze. Rain streaks them and pentagrams are engraved as their eyes; Dolmenwood natives recognize them as Drune symbols.
fields.title: Thirteen Iron Owls

fields.description: The forested area around Sir Chyde's burial mound, where random supernatural or woodland events are checked every two turns.
fields.title: Outside the Mound

fields.description: A burial mound in the glade beside the Whything Stones. It includes Sir Chyde's burial, a subsection dedicated to his betrothed, and a chapel of St Sedge. Once maintained as a pilgrimage site, it was later warded and sealed after fey influence and hauntings.
fields.title: Sir Chyde's Tomb

fields.description: An ancient stone circle in a Dolmenwood clearing where Sir Chyde and Snowfall-at-Dusk first met. Its mossy stones bear moonlight-reflecting eldritch runes and hidden carvings of tormented icy fey; the Drune now frequent and guard the site.
fields.title: The Whything Stones

steps: Place the adventure in a cool region where icy fairies and rings of ancient standing stones are plausible.
Integrate the background into the chosen setting.
Replace the Cold Prince with another wicked fairy king when appropriate.
fields.title: Adapt the Adventure to Another Setting
fields.trigger: The referee is running the adventure outside Dolmenwood.

steps: Check for a random event with a 1-in-6 chance.
If an event occurs, use one of the four entries in the Outside the Mound random event table and resolve its stated mechanics.
fields.title: Check Random Events Outside the Mound
fields.trigger: The party spends two turns outside the burial mound.

steps: Employ sages, search obscure tomes, or consult oracles.
Treat each hidden fact as requiring its own significant research effort.
Reveal, as research succeeds, the Lady's identity, the ring's nature, the notable grave goods, and the reason the tomb was sealed.
fields.title: Research the True Story
fields.trigger: PCs spend substantial time and money investigating Sir Chyde and the Lady.

steps: In a second dream, the PC sees themself enter a burial mound, open a coffer, remove a ring from a skeleton's finger, and bring it to the Lady.
The Lady says the tomb is real and that a magical door to her realm lies on its lower level.
She falsely promises her heart if the PC retrieves the ring that she says was stolen from her in ancient times.
She reveals the tomb's location and says a bearer of the ring can enter the lower-level door into her realm in Fairy.
fields.title: Follow the Lady's Dream Instructions
fields.trigger: The chosen PC has experienced the recurring romantic dream for several weeks.

steps: Review an old charter and family tree claiming that the PC descends from Brigford the Wise, Sir Chyde's brother.
Use the charter to locate the tomb where Brigford is interred beside his brother.
Note the charter's claim that Sir Chyde's fabled sword and ring legally belong to the inheriting PC.
Note the documents' claim that the ring can open a doorway to Fairy.
fields.title: Investigate the Inherited Charter
fields.trigger: The PC receives the deceased relative's papers and oddments.

steps: Choose any forest hex outside the Witching Ring, Chell.
Treat the adventure's events as independent of any specific established location in the forest.
fields.title: Place the Adventure in Dolmenwood
fields.trigger: The referee is using Winter's Daughter in a Dolmenwood campaign.

steps: Use the wizard's map to reach the old burial mound in Dolmenwood.
Enter the tomb.
Take the bronze, moonstone-set ring with woven-branch fittings from the finger of the buried skeleton.
Return the ring to the wizard for 5,000 gp, or another reward amount chosen by the referee.
fields.title: Recover the Ring for the Wizard
fields.trigger: The PCs accept the wizard's employment.

fields.text: The adventure is intended for 1st- to 3rd-level PCs. Encounters are not all balanced to the party's capabilities; play should favor discretion and the judicious use of stealth, parley, and trickery rather than blindly entering combat.
fields.title: Character Levels and Encounter Approach

fields.text: Fairies are especially vulnerable to weapons forged from pure iron and suffer double damage when such a weapon hits successfully.
fields.title: Pure Iron Against Fairies

fields.text: The touch of mortal silver repulses and sickens fairies. The delicate, pale silver native to Fairy does not produce this effect.
fields.title: Silver Sickness

fields.text: The referee needs Old-School Essentials to run the adventure; both Classic Fantasy and Advanced Fantasy are suitable. The classic Basic/Expert game or another derived ruleset may be used instead.
fields.title: Supported Rulesets
Cold Prince Campaign Arc
fields.trigger: Investigative PCs uncover secrets about the war between mortals and fairies roughly nine centuries ago; the referee may connect those discoveries to the banished Cold Prince's attempts to return and claim Dolmenwood.

fields.title: Defeat and Exile of the Cold Prince
fields.trigger: Mortal armies win the war and exile the Cold Prince to his dominion in Fairy. He has not openly troubled Dolmenwood since, but common folk fear his return; folklore says the banishing magic weakens each winter and frigid winds whisper of his desire to reclaim the mortal kingdom.

fields.title: Forbidden Love of Mortal and Fairy
fields.trigger: During the war, Sir Chyde and Princess Snowfall-at-Dusk meet beside the Whything Stones and begin secret trysts. Chyde commissions the portrait The Lady of the Wood, and the princess gives him a magical ring that binds their souls together for eternity.

fields.title: Hook: Dreams of the Lady
fields.trigger: A valiant or courageous PC begins receiving recurring dreams from a beautiful elf lady dressed in white and wakes with a profound yearning to be with her.

fields.title: Hook: Inheritance
fields.trigger: An elderly, long-lost relative of a PC dies and leaves the PC minor wealth, old papers, and an apparent hereditary claim connected to Sir Chyde's tomb.

fields.title: Hook: Tomb Robbers
fields.trigger: A wizard hires the PCs to travel into Dolmenwood and rob an old burial mound.

fields.title: Perpetual Wedding Feast
fields.trigger: Still determined to marry Sir Chyde despite his death and the passing centuries, Snowfall-at-Dusk maintains a perpetual wedding feast in her isolated tower. A few brave friends and allies have secretly joined the delayed festivities while she awaits him.

fields.title: Princess Imprisoned
fields.trigger: The Cold Prince discovers his daughter's relationship with Sir Chyde. His spies capture her, and he confines her in a forlorn tower until she renounces the love; through the binding ring, she secretly continues speaking with Chyde and they plan her rescue.

fields.title: Death and Burial of Sir Chyde
fields.trigger: Sir Chyde is slain in the final battle shortly after Snowfall-at-Dusk is imprisoned. He asks to be interred in a tomb by the Whything Stones with the portrait and ring, with a tomb section for his betrothed and a chapel of St Sedge; the tomb later serves as a pilgrimage site with a resident priest.

fields.title: Sealing of Sir Chyde's Tomb
fields.trigger: An unsettling fey influence enters the tomb, and its priest suffers disturbing dreams and visitations. The priest recommends abandonment; guardians and wards are installed, and the tomb is sealed.

fields.title: Touching an Iron Owl
fields.trigger: When a character touches one of the thirteen iron owls, a chill comes over that character.

fields.title: Twisted Trees Close Behind the Party
fields.trigger: As PCs pass through the tangled forest toward the burial mound, the twisted trees seem to close in and block the way out.

fields.title: Twitching Stag Skeleton and Green Haze
fields.trigger: A slime-coated stag skeleton twitches among the stones while bright green, glowing slime evaporates into a lingering haze. Breathing the acrid haze makes a character light-headed.

entries.result: A PC notices a ghostly, violet-eyed owl watching from a high branch. That PC must save versus spells or faint for 1d6 turns.

1d4 tipsy goblin merchants carrying lanterns cautiously emerge from a forest-floor trapdoor. They have crossed from Fairy into Dolmenwood while searching for rare night-fruits; see Dolmenwood Goblin, page 20.

A gust drives nearby branches into a frenzy. PCs close to trees must save versus paralysis or take 1 damage. Flames sputter and may extinguish: torches have a 4-in-6 chance and lanterns a 2-in-6 chance to go out.
A huge, warty toad approaches, studies the PCs, and croaks the single word 'Betrayal'.

fields.title: Outside the Mound Random Events (1-in-6 Chance Every Two Turns)

fields.role: Two moisture-slick skeletons waltz arm in arm in mid-air above the fissure. One wears a pearl necklace and the other a gold medallion, each worth 500gp. They welcome strangers to join the dance, speak old-fashioned Woldish (Common, not Old Woldish) in a distant whisper, and attack vehemently if any coffer is disturbed. Statistics: AC 8 [11], HD 2 (hp 8, 10), Att 1 × claws (1d4), THAC0 18 [+1], MV 90’ (30’) flying, SV D12 W13 P14 B15 S16 (2), ML 12, AL Neutral, XP 20. As undead they are unaffected by charms and mind control. Any weapon that hits one in melee becomes weightless for a moment, imposing –1 to that weapon's attack roll in the next round.
fields.title: Floating Skeletons

fields.role: A pale, semi-transparent azure, thin, plate-armoured ghost with raised visor, forlorn and love-lost, kneels before the portrait. He beseeches the characters to help him reach his beloved in Fairy and does not appreciate tomb robbers. Statistics: AC 3 [16], HD 5* (26 hp), Att 1 × touch (1d6 + aging), THAC0 15 [+4], MV 60’ (20’), SV D10 W11 P12 B13 S14 (5), ML 11, AL Lawful, XP 300. His touch ages a mortal target 2d20 years; a fairy does not age but must save versus spells or suffer terror for 1d6 rounds. As incorporeal undead, he is harmed only by magic or silver and is unaffected by charms and mind control. Turning makes him disappear for 24 hours. He is tethered to the ring in the coffer and cannot exist more than 10 feet from it.
fields.title: The Ghost of Sir Chyde

fields.role: The four mould-covered religious objects animate as flying attackers and shrill, sanctimonious scolds, condemning the characters' misdeeds, including entering the tomb. Statistics: AC 5 [14], HD 1 (hp 3, 3, 4, 5), Att 1 × bash (1d4), THAC0 19 [0], MV 90’ (30’) flying, SV D12 W13 P14 B15 S16 (1), ML 12, AL Lawful, XP 10. When one is killed, it erupts in mould spores; anyone in melee must save versus poison or suffer 1d2 damage and choke for 1 round, during which they cannot act.
fields.title: Religious Objects

fields.role: Two 6-foot-tall stone constructs guard the doors in area 12. Statistics: AC 3 [16], HD 4* (hp 17, 19), Att 1 × bite (1d8), THAC0 16 [+3], MV 120’ (40’), SV D10 W11 P12 B13 S14 (4), ML 12, AL Neutral, XP 125. Their chains prevent them from leaving the room. As constructs, they are harmed only by magic and are unaffected by charms and mind control.
fields.title: Stone Hounds

fields.role: Three 4-foot-long, thigh-thick, dark-pink, bumpy, eyeless worms with lamprey-like tooth-ringed mouths lurk in the narrow tunnel by area 10 and can be attracted or disturbed from area 4. They attack by taste and ravenously attack when noise disturbs them. Statistics: AC 7 [12], HD 1+1* (hp 3, 4, 5), Att 1 × bite (1d4 + acid), THAC0 18 [+1], MV 120’ (40’), SV D12 W13 P14 B15 S16 (1), ML 7, AL Neutral, XP 19. Their acid causes 1 damage per round until washed off, for example with water.
fields.title: Wormtongues

fields.text: The mural depicts Sir Chyde mounted in battle against a fairy army, accompanied by two hunting hounds. When cleared, his raised hand is shown holding the same wavy-grooved longsword as the statue weapon, glowing white, and one hound's collar gives the name Chedr.
fields.title: Battle mural clue naming Chedr

fields.text: The statues hold: a flanged mace with a spiralling hilt; a morningstar with 2-inch spikes; a battle axe engraved with a horse's head; a warhammer whose head is shaped like a boar; a longsword with wavy blood grooves; a halberd with a mouldy pennant; and a spear with a serrated blade. The fairy-made longsword is enchanted, granting +2 to hit and damage. Its glamour affects mortal wielders and compels them to attack the largest foe in battle.
fields.title: Weapons held by the seven footmen

fields.text: The stone coffer is carved with Sir Chyde's likeness and leaf patterns and contains his skeleton. On its wrists are two copper bracelets engraved with owls whose amethyst eyes make each bracelet worth 1,000gp. On one finger is a bronze band set with a moonstone and branch-like fittings: the Ring of Soul-Binding. The restored portrait is worth 1,500gp. Each cleaned silver candlestick is worth 200gp.
fields.title: Sir Chyde’s coffer, portrait, and candlesticks

fields.text: The tapestry shows Sir Chyde and St Sedge meeting at the gates of heaven after death. A locked, damp-swollen wooden door is hidden behind it.
fields.title: Chapel tapestry and concealed door

fields.text: The writing desk's locked drawer is easily smashed open. Inside is an old mould-covered book whose damp-stuck pages are indecipherable, but a brass sheet inside the cover bears a pastoral poem about Sir Chyde hunting with his favoured dogs. One dog is named Flaegr.
fields.title: Pastoral poem naming Flaegr

fields.text: The mirror has 1,000gp material value. If removed from the tomb, its magical properties fade after one month.
fields.title: Freezing mirror value and persistence

fields.text: The mosaic shows Sir Chyde on a white charger piercing a fairy knight's heart. Its Old Woldish inscription reads, “Here lies the noble Sir Chyde, slayer of Frost, defender of the King”. Speakers of modern Woldish can recognize the name and the words for “Frost” and “King”. Scratches indicate that something heavy was dragged from area 7 a long time ago.
fields.title: Hall of Guardians mosaic and drag marks

fields.text: The locked metal box contains a silver crucifix worth 50gp, a clerical scroll of hold person, a stamped-gold-leaf prayer book worth 500gp, and a box of 20 magically preserved holy wafers. Each wafer cures 1hp.
fields.title: Contents of the priest’s hidden box

fields.text: Sir Chyde knows that the stairs in areas 6 and 7 provide entrance to Fairy. He believes the princess awaits there, imprisoned, and wants at last to take her hand in marriage after centuries apart.
fields.title: Sir Chyde’s knowledge of Fairy

fields.text: The apparent vaulted pool is the tomb's bottom level as perceived before passing through the ward in the mortal world. Centuries of action by the Ring of Soul-Binding have warped reality so that Fairy is now more present here than the mortal world. The Church placed the stair-bottom wards when sealing the tomb to prevent further encroachment from Fairy.
fields.title: Warped reality at the Warded Pool

fields.description: A granite slab seals the burial mound and is overgrown with lichen and sweet-smelling wild roses. Beyond it, stairs descend 20 feet into the earth through centuries of undisturbed dust, deathly silence, and a moist, mouldy smell. Scratches on the stairs indicate that something heavy was dragged upward long ago.
fields.title: 3. Tomb Entrance

fields.description: A barely 2-foot-wide hole at the mound's edge burrows into the earth and emerges after 15 feet in area 10. Gooey, opalescent, largely transparent slime trails, like petroleum jelly, run from the hole into the woods and back.
fields.title: 4. Worm Hole

fields.description: A musty, wet chamber with dank, stifling air and wet walls and ceiling. Four approximately 1-foot-tall religious objects stand on corner plinths under mustard-coloured mould: a silver crucifix worth 200gp, a wooden cherub statue, a holy book, and a huge candle. Heavy damp-streaked stone double doors bear the inscription “The Most Dear”. The dusty floor conceals a mosaic and old drag scratches.
fields.title: 5. Hall of Guardians

fields.description: A white-marble statue depicts a fair maiden with long flowing hair and robe, a star on her brow, and one finger raised to her lips in a plea for silence. A black cloth blindfold covers its eyes. The statue stands on a 3-foot-wide, 1-foot-high round marble plinth. Pristine stairs descend toward area 14 beneath an arch carved as interwoven tree branches; illumination reveals reflections shimmering from water below.
fields.title: 6. Blindfolded Statue

fields.description: A full-length mirror in a beautifully wrought silver frame engraved with crucifixes and unicorns at play hangs behind an empty 3-foot-wide, 1-foot-high white-marble statue plinth. Floor scratches show that a heavy statue was dragged toward area 5. Pristine stairs descend toward area 14 under an interwoven-tree stone arch; illumination reveals water reflections below.
fields.title: 7. Freezing Mirror

fields.description: Two floating skeletons dance above a fissure in a family crypt containing five stone coffers with tarnished brass portrait plaques. Coffers A and B are open with their lids pushed aside. Transparent slime drips from a hairline ceiling crack, coats the skeletons, and falls into a fissure of initially indeterminate depth; glimmering light below resembles sunlight reflected from snow.
fields.title: 8. Family Crypt

fields.description: A decaying but once-solid set of wooden pews faces a stone altar. The altar bears a statue of St Sedge, a holy crusader holding a thick red candle aloft; dried red wax has run over the statue and altar, and the velvet cloth is disintegrating. A ragged tapestry depicts the gates of heaven, where Sir Chyde and St Sedge meet in death. A locked wooden door, swollen with damp, is concealed behind the tapestry.
fields.title: 9. Chapel of St Sedge

fields.description: A damp-swollen locked wooden door opens onto abandoned quarters. A collapsed wall leaves rubble, dark earth, and a 2-foot-wide tunnel climbing toward area 4. A decaying angel-carved writing desk holds a stuck, mould-covered book. A loose flagstone conceals a small space with a locked metal box.
fields.title: 10. Abandoned Priest’s Quarters

fields.description: Seven smooth, finely carved dark-stone statues of footmen hold real weapons. The walls bear vivid yellow and purple mould patches. A faded mural shows Sir Chyde on horseback fighting a fairy army with two hunting hounds at his side; mould obscures his raised right hand and parts of the hounds.
fields.title: 11. Statues With Weapons

fields.description: Pillars carved with scenes of holy war against fairies flank massive, smooth stone double doors. The doors are locked and magically warded, with “Call to the Companions” cut deeply into them. Two larger-than-life, 6-foot-tall stone hounds are chained to the base of the doors.
fields.title: 12. Hall of Hounds

fields.description: Sir Chyde's ghost kneels before a dust-grimed portrait of a fair blond maiden in a white robe with a star on her brow, standing amid the Whything Stones of area 2. A carved stone coffer holds the knight's skeleton and grave goods. Two 4-foot-tall tarnished silver candlesticks stand on the floor.
fields.title: 13. The Knight’s Tomb

fields.description: From the mortal side, area 14 appears as a vaulted chamber filled by a shimmering pool, with a white-marble statue of a long-haired, robed maiden bearing a star on her brow at its centre. At the foot of the stairs, dozens of ghostly candles float in mid-air and form an unavoidable ward.
fields.title: 14. Warded Pool

steps: Clearing the knight’s hand reveals a longsword with wavy blood grooves surrounded by a white glow.
Clearing the hounds reveals the name Chedr written on one hound’s collar.
Resolve disturbance of the mould using its poison-spore hazard.
fields.title: Clear mould from the battle mural
fields.trigger: Characters remove mould from Sir Chyde's raised hand or the painted hounds.

steps: Cover the mirror to bypass its freezing effect.
Unfreeze an affected person with holy water, cure light wounds, or sunlight.
fields.title: Bypass or reverse the freezing mirror
fields.trigger: Characters need to pass the mirror safely or free someone frozen by it.

steps: Feel a wave of religious awe.
The perceived vaulted chamber dissolves and reforms as an outdoor scene with a white tower on an island in a frozen lake.
Appear in area 15.
fields.title: Pass through the candle ward into Fairy
fields.trigger: A character coming from area 6 or area 7 passes through the ghostly candles at the bottom step.

steps: Fairy magic cannot dispel the ward.
Other magic can dispel it; treat the ward as if cast by a 10th-level cleric.
fields.title: Dispel the candle ward
fields.trigger: Characters attempt to dispel the ward at the bottom of the stairs.

steps: Find scratches showing that something heavy was dragged up the stairs a long time ago.
fields.title: Examine the stairs into the mound
fields.trigger: Characters closely examine the stairs in area 3.

steps: A character skilled in tracking can identify trails of three slug- or worm-like creatures leading from the hole into the woods and back.
Bare-flesh contact reveals slight acidity, but the slime is not acidic enough to inflict damage.
fields.title: Examine the worm-hole slime trails
fields.trigger: Characters track or touch the slime trails by area 4.

steps: Locate the loose flagstone.
Lift it to reveal a small space containing a locked metal box.
fields.title: Find the cache beneath the loose flagstone
fields.trigger: Characters search area 10 for secret doors or traps.

steps: Take the bronze moonstone ring from the stone coffer.
Carry it to the lower tomb level at area 14.
Use the stairs in area 6 or area 7 to enter Fairy, where Sir Chyde believes the imprisoned princess waits.
fields.title: Carry Sir Chyde’s ring toward his beloved
fields.trigger: The ghost asks a living person to help him join the princess in Fairy.

steps: See shimmering reflections from water below.
fields.title: Illuminate the stairs to area 14
fields.trigger: Characters shine light down the pristine stairs in area 6 or area 7.

steps: Catch glimpses of glimmering light below, like sunlight reflected off snow.
fields.title: Look into the family-crypt fissure
fields.trigger: Characters gaze down into the fissure in area 8.

steps: Illumination reveals a 15-foot descent to area 10.
Making noise attracts the wormtongues lurking inside.
Crawling down disturbs the wormtongues and leads to area 10 after 15 feet.
fields.title: Investigate or enter the worm hole
fields.trigger: Characters illuminate the hole, make noise near it, or crawl down it.

steps: A wind rushes through the chapel, followed by distant neighing and victorious battle cries.
fields.title: Light St Sedge’s candle
fields.trigger: Characters light the thick red candle held by the statue on the chapel altar.

steps: Speak the names “Flaegr and Chedr”, in either order.
The doors open when both names are spoken.
fields.title: Answer the Hall of Hounds riddle
fields.trigger: Characters attempt to open the locked, magically warded double doors in area 12.

steps: Move the slab with a cumulative STR bonus of at least 4.
Alternatively, break the slab over 6 turns; cumulative STR bonuses reduce this time, to a minimum of 2 turns.
fields.title: Open the tomb entrance slab
fields.trigger: Characters attempt to move or break the granite slab sealing area 3.

steps: Discover golden crucifixes embroidered on the inside of the cloth.
fields.title: Remove the blindfold from the maiden statue
fields.trigger: Characters unwrap the black cloth from the statue in area 6.

steps: Characters who originally came from the tomb can pass back through.
The ward is impassable to others.
fields.title: Return through the candle ward
fields.trigger: A character in Fairy attempts to pass back through the ward toward the tomb.

steps: Disturbing the dust reveals colours beneath it.
Clearing the floor exposes a mosaic and scratches indicating old heavy movement.
fields.title: Reveal the Hall of Guardians mosaic
fields.trigger: Movement disturbs the dusty floor in area 5, or characters deliberately clear it.

steps: Pass the three lurking wormtongues and emerge at area 4.
fields.title: Crawl through the priest’s-quarters tunnel
fields.trigger: Characters crawl upward through the narrow tunnel behind the collapsed wall in area 10.

fields.title: Disturbed mould releases choking spores
fields.trigger: Disturbing the yellow-and-purple wall mould raises a spore cloud; everyone within 10 feet must save versus poison or suffer 1d4 damage and violent coughing and choking for 1 turn.

fields.title: Fairy characters sense the ageless realm
fields.trigger: At the bottom of the stairs, fairy player characters feel the presence of the ageless realm pressing against the ward from the other side.

fields.title: The dancing skeletons defend the coffers
fields.trigger: If any coffer in area 8 is disturbed, both floating skeletons attack vehemently.

fields.title: The fissure transports descendents into Fairy
fields.trigger: A person or object descends more than 15 feet into the fissure; it then drifts harmlessly, snowflake-like, down from the sky in Fairy at area 15, even though the fall seems long.

fields.title: The slime vapour removes weight
fields.trigger: An object touching the slime becomes weightless for a moment. If bare flesh touches it, the slime instantly coats the character's whole body; the character becomes permanently lighter than air and drifts to the ceiling until the slime is removed, for example by dispel magic.

fields.title: The freezing mirror immobilizes passersby
fields.trigger: Anyone who passes in front of the mirror must save versus paralysis or be frozen still.

fields.title: Unanswered door contact animates the hounds
fields.trigger: Touching the doors without first answering the riddle causes both stone hounds to animate and attack.

fields.title: Poison needle on the hidden box
fields.trigger: Opening or manipulating the hidden metal box lock triggers a poison needle; the victim must save versus poison or suffer 1d6 damage and fall unconscious for 1d6 turns.

fields.title: Religious objects attack non-Lawful intruders
fields.trigger: When a non-Lawful character sets foot in area 5, the four objects float into the air and attack.

fields.title: Crushing the Ring of Soul-Binding
fields.trigger: If the ring is crushed, its power ends, Sir Chyde's soul is released, and the ghost disappears into the afterlife.

fields.title: Removing the Ring of Soul-Binding
fields.trigger: When the ring is removed from the coffer, Sir Chyde's ghost disappears temporarily. It can manifest once per day and haunt the person who stole the ring. The ghost remains tethered to the ring and cannot exist more than 10 feet from it.

fields.title: Noise rouses the wormtongues
fields.trigger: Noise in area 10 disturbs the three wormtongues lurking in the tunnel by the collapsed wall, and they ravenously attack.

entries.result: A vision of a beautiful woman dressed all in white, with a star upon her brow, appears in empty space and says, “The ring… The ring holds the key… My eternal salvation”, before disappearing into mist.
The sound of hounds baying echoes through the crypt.
The 2 dancing skeletons from area 8 waltz through the air on a tour of the tomb.
1d3 wormtongues break through a wall or ceiling, hungry for living flesh; see Wormtongues, p15.

fields.title: The Burial Mound — Random Events (1-in-6 Chance Every Two Turns)

entries.name: Lady Amaranda
entries.portrait: Tall, elegant, stick-like, with a big nose, holding a book.

entries.name: Lord Brigforwith
entries.portrait: Stocky, with a round head and chunky beard.

entries.name: Brandywith the Good
entries.portrait: Bespectacled, head bowed, leaning on a staff.

entries.name: Brigford the Wise
entries.portrait: In chainmail, with a hound at his side and a bow in hand.

entries.name: Emaline the Chaste
entries.portrait: Petite, in a mourning veil, cradling a cat.

entries.contents: A skeleton with an ash staff.
A skeleton dressed in rusted mail.
Two skeletons: one human and one feline.

fields.role: A pack of 2d6 dire wolves may creep from the forest and sniff around the frozen lake for prey; use the dire wolf statistics from Old-School Essentials.
fields.title: Dire Wolf Pack

fields.role: Two short, stout, blue-skinned cooks with twinkling pearly eyes. They are flustered but orderly and loudly order intruders to help carry food to the feast. Combat profile: AC 9 [10], HD 1 (3 hp each), attack 1 × knife or rolling pin (1d3), THAC0 19 [0], MV 120’ (40’), saves D12 W13 P13 B15 S15 (E1), ML 6, Neutral, XP 10 each.
fields.title: Frost Elf Cooks

fields.role: Proud frost elf warriors who serve as guests and guards. A random event may bring 1d3 knights from the forest on white chargers; at the feast, 5 knights sit as guests and 4 guards stand at the edges, ready to act. Combat profile: AC 3 [16], HD 2, attack 1 × spear or lance (1d6), THAC0 18 [+1], MV 60’ (20’), saves D12 W13 P13 B15 S15 (E2), ML 9, Neutral, XP 20.
fields.title: Frost Elf Guards and Knights

fields.role: Seven decadent, foppish nobles in flouncy silk and lace, quietly sipping wine and dabbing handkerchiefs. They are ambivalent toward strangers but call the guards if disturbed. Combat profile: AC 8 [11], HD 4*, attack 1 × icicle dagger (1d4) or 1 × spell, THAC0 16 [+3], MV 120’ (40’), saves D10 W11 P11 B13 S12 (E4), ML 7, Neutral, XP 125; spells sleep and hold person.
fields.title: Frost Elf Nobles

fields.role: A goblin courier who may race from the forest in a laden sleigh pulled by white stags, bringing fairy fruits, ice wines, and a cauldron of steaming soup to the tower.
fields.title: Goblin Sleigh-Rider

fields.role: A jovial Dolmenwood goblin doorman with a large head, spindly neck, dark grey warty skin, huge yellow eyes, and purple velvet finery. He rides on Grimmlegridge’s back, checks every visitor’s name, admits invited wedding guests, and offers uninvited visitors entry if they eat a mushroom from his pouch. Combat profile: AC 7 [12], HD 1* (4 hp), attack 1 × spear (1d6) or 1 × spell, THAC0 19 [0], MV 90’ (30’), saves D12 W13 P14 B15 S16 (1), ML 7, Neutral, XP 13; spells charm person, darkness, sleep, and phantasmal force.
fields.title: Griddlegrim

fields.role: A hulking, obese, 10-foot-tall Dolmenwood troll with hairless clay-like flesh, filthy ragged hessian clothes, and a bulging pouch of moss-covered humanoid bones. He obeys Griddlegrim but secretly wants to crush the characters and add their bodies to his moss-corpse collection. Combat profile: AC 6 [13], HD 8* (45 hp), attacks 2 × fists (1d10 plus moss growth), THAC0 12 [+7], MV 120’ (40’), saves D8 W9 P10 B10 S12 (8), ML 9, Chaotic, XP 1,200. A touched mortal sprouts moss at the contact point. He regenerates 3 hp per round and reforms unless killed with fire or acid.
fields.title: Grimmlegridge

fields.role: An ageless, benevolent frost elf princess with winter-sun blonde hair, scintillating pale skin, crystalline blue eyes, a flowing white gown, and a crystal star bound to her brow. She is dignified, hopeful despite her imprisonment, and excited by the possibilities presented by mortal strangers. She wants reunion with Sir Chyde. Combat profile: AC 7 [12], HD 5* (19 hp), attack 1 × icicle dagger (1d4) or 1 × spell, THAC0 15 [+4], MV 120’ (40’), saves D10 W11 P11 B13 S12 (E5), ML 8, Neutral, XP 300; spells charm person, sleep, hold person, and invisibility. She can grant one other person’s wish, but may use that power only once ever.
fields.title: Princess Snowfall-at-Dusk

fields.role: A cawing white raven that arrives during a random event carrying a message for Princess Snowfall-at-Dusk: her friend Lord Mantle-of-Runes is coming.
fields.title: White Raven Messenger

fields.text: The first mushroom a character eats each day produces one random magical effect determined by 1d12. Unless the rolled entry states otherwise, that effect is permanent.
fields.title: First Mushroom of the Day

fields.text: Removing mushrooms never empties the pouch; it is always full.
fields.title: Limitless Mushrooms

fields.text: Any mushrooms eaten after the first one on the same day make the character sick rather than producing another random effect.
fields.title: Additional Mushroom Sickness

fields.text: The ring’s possessor may give it to another person, binding that person’s soul to the giver’s. An unwilling recipient receives a save versus spells to resist.
fields.title: Soul Binding

fields.text: The two bound persons can communicate verbally through the ring.
fields.title: Ring-Borne Communication

fields.text: On a full-moon night, the wearer may call the other bound person to them. The pair are physically united for one night.
fields.title: Full-Moon Union

fields.text: If the ring’s wearer dies, their spirit cannot rest and haunts the ring as a ghost. The ghost can manifest only while within 10 feet of the ring.
fields.title: Ghost Bound to the Ring

fields.text: When one bound person is in the mortal world and the other is in Fairy, the ring draws them closer by narrowing the boundary between the two worlds.
fields.title: Planar Boundary Narrowing

fields.text: The bond ends if the ring is destroyed; dispel magic is cast on the ring or either bound person; either bound person renounces the binding; or the person who gave the ring dies.
fields.title: Undoing the Soul Binding

fields.text: The eater doubles in size, destroying their clothing, and deals double melee damage for 1d6 turns.
fields.title: Double Size

fields.text: The eater shrinks to 6 inches tall for 1d6 turns.
fields.title: Six-Inch Stature

fields.text: The eater’s skin turns permanently purple.
fields.title: Purple Skin

fields.text: The eater’s eyes shrivel away; 1 turn later, new eyes grow in the palms of their hands.
fields.title: Eyes in the Palms

fields.text: All hair on the eater’s body grows to 10 feet long.
fields.title: Ten-Foot Hair

fields.text: The eater’s nose swells, develops a sour face, becomes sentient, and endlessly criticizes the character’s actions.
fields.title: Sentient Critical Nose

fields.text: Increase one randomly selected ability score by +1.
fields.title: Random Ability Increase

fields.text: The eater’s eyes enlarge and emit yellow light in a 30-foot radius.
fields.title: Luminous Enlarged Eyes

fields.text: The eater automatically succeeds on their next saving throw.
fields.title: Warm Fuzzy Assurance

fields.text: The eater’s body becomes transparent for 1d6 turns. If naked, the character surprises on a roll of 1–4.
fields.title: Transparent Body

fields.text: Whenever spoken to, the eater alternates between weeping and hysterical laughter for 1d6 turns.
fields.title: Weeping and Hysterical Laughter

fields.text: The eater vomits a stream of worms and maggots and can do nothing else for 1d6 turns.
fields.title: Vomit Worms and Maggots

fields.text: The princess’s jewellery boxes contain 12 necklaces of fairy silver, each worth 150 gp.
fields.title: Necklaces of Fairy Silver

fields.text: The princess’s wardrobe holds 20 fur coats, each worth 100 gp.
fields.title: Fur Coats

fields.text: A sapphire set in a platinum brooch shaped like spiky hoarfrost; worth 1,000 gp.
fields.title: Hoarfrost Sapphire Brooch

fields.text: The princess’s jewellery boxes contain 30 ice-jewels, each worth 200 gp.
fields.title: Ice-Jewels

fields.text: An ordinary-looking burlap belt pouch filled with colourful mushrooms. It never runs out. The first mushroom a character eats each day produces a random magical effect on 1d12; later mushrooms that day make the character sick. Unless an entry says otherwise, the effect is permanent.
fields.title: Pouch of Limitless Fungi

fields.text: A flashing crystal star bound to the princess’s brow with a silver cord; worth 300 gp.
fields.title: Princess Snowfall-at-Dusk’s Brow Star

fields.text: A fairy magic ring that intertwines two beings’ souls. Its bearer may give it to another person to bind them; an unwilling recipient may save versus spells. The binding ends if the ring is destroyed, dispel magic is cast on the ring or either bound person, either person renounces the bond, or the giver dies. Bound persons can speak through the ring; cross-world separation narrows the boundary between Fairy and the mortal world; on a full moon the wearer can call the other person to them for one night; if the wearer dies, their spirit haunts the ring as a ghost able to manifest only within 10 feet of it.
fields.title: Ring of Soul-Binding

fields.text: The princess’s wardrobe holds 20 scintillating gowns, each worth 100 gp. The wardrobe contains more garments than should physically fit inside.
fields.title: Scintillating Gowns

fields.text: The frost elf cooks know that Princess Snowfall-at-Dusk’s guests are waiting for the arrival of her betrothed, Sir Chyde.
fields.title: The Feast Awaits Sir Chyde

fields.text: Dolmenwood goblins are native to Fairy. In the mortal world they are known as tricksters, charlatans, and sellers of strange fey objects.
fields.title: Dolmenwood Goblin Lore

fields.text: Dolmenwood trolls are mossivorous fairies. Their preferred food is moss grown on the corpse of a sentient being, a taste that drives them to murder.
fields.title: Dolmenwood Troll Lore

fields.text: Reuniting Sir Chyde and Princess Snowfall-at-Dusk does not remove the magic imprisoning her in the tower. Deeper magic or the Cold Prince’s intervention would be required.
fields.title: Reunion Does Not Break the Princess’s Ban

fields.text: Sir Chyde or Princess Snowfall-at-Dusk may later find a way to contact the characters and ask for help breaking the princess’s magical imprisonment.
fields.title: Possible Future Plea from the Lovers

fields.text: The Cold Prince continually seeks a return to Dolmenwood. A doorway in his own kingdom leading there would be priceless, and the characters could exploit the route for schemes beyond the adventure.
fields.title: The Cold Prince’s Interest in the Door

fields.text: The wards set when Sir Chyde’s tomb was sealed stop natives of Frigia from passing between Fairy and the mortal world, but mortals may travel from Dolmenwood into Frigia. Fairy magic cannot dispel these wards, though mortal magic may be able to do so.
fields.title: Wards Between the Tomb and Frigia

fields.text: Princess Snowfall-at-Dusk cannot leave the glade containing her tower unless she renounces her love for Sir Chyde. The ban also defeats magical summoning and teleportation, including the Ring of Soul-Binding’s full-moon power to unite bound persons.
fields.title: The Princess’s Magical Ban

fields.text: The princess knows that Sir Chyde’s soul remains in his tomb, that his hounds are named Chedr and Flaegr, and that the warded paths from her glade lead to the tomb in the mortal world. She believes he was taken from her by mortality.
fields.title: Princess Snowfall-at-Dusk’s Knowledge of Sir Chyde

fields.description: A lake frozen solid to a depth of 5 feet, with a cleared ice-skating patch. The white marble tower stands on it.
fields.title: Frozen Lake

fields.description: An ominous fir wood heavy with snow. Moss-covered corpses hang in the trees as food for the troll Grimmlegridge. The fairy woods are treacherous and may contain giant spiders, frost elves, or winter wolves.
fields.title: Hoar-Clad Forest

fields.description: A purple crack hangs in the sky and occasionally sheds sticky purple drips that stain the snow.
fields.title: Purple Crack in the Sky

fields.description: Forest paths are blocked by dozens of ghostly candles floating in mid-air. A traveller cannot step onto a path without passing through the candle ward.
fields.title: Paths into the Forest

fields.description: A white marble tower with icy walls that impose –20% on checks to climb sheer surfaces. Its polished cherrywood door with black iron fittings is unlocked; frost-patterned windows can be smashed open; a thin bluish smoke plume rises from the summit.
fields.title: White Marble Tower

fields.description: A bitterly cold glade under gently falling snow, with pristine 2-foot-deep snow, sparkling sunlight, and visible breath. Larger-than-human bootprints run from the tower to the woods and back.
fields.title: Wintry Glade

fields.description: The tower entrance is decorated with garlands of white roses and pale blue forget-me-nots tied with ribbons. Dozens of winter hats and coats crowd wall hooks; boots and ice skates line shoe racks. A fireplace burns melting icicles with electric-blue flames. Baking aromas drift from area 17, while muted voices come from the stairs to area 18.
fields.title: Entrance Hall

fields.description: A busy kitchen with an electric-blue icicle fire, a cast-iron stove holding bubbling stockpots and baking currant buns, a flour-covered worktable, and a pantry packed with candied fruit, frozen game, and ice wines. The air smells of currants and spice and is thick with broth steam.
fields.title: Fairy Kitchen

fields.description: A lavish feast room dominated by a table laden with roast swans stuffed with blackbirds, syrup-dripping fruit, ice wines in buckets, and violet spirits in crystal decanters. Five frost elf knights and seven frost elf nobles wait in subdued silence; the princess’s guests have already waited for centuries.
fields.title: Wedding Feast

fields.description: A regal chamber with a canopy bed veiled in snow dust and covered in white wolf skins, a dressing table with jewellery boxes, an overfull wardrobe of coats and gowns, and a fireplace of melting icicles burning with electric-blue flames.
fields.title: The Princess’s Bedchamber

fields.description: The tower stands in an obscure part of Frigia, the Cold Prince’s fairy kingdom. The Ring of Soul-Binding has drawn this region close to the mortal world over centuries, creating a usable route from Dolmenwood into Fairy.
fields.title: A Door to Frigia

steps: Fairy magic cannot affect the ward.
Other magic may dispel it.
Resolve dispelling as though the ward were cast by a 10th-level cleric.
fields.title: Dispel the Ghostly Candle Ward
fields.trigger: Someone attempts to remove the ward blocking the forest paths.

steps: A character who came from the tomb can pass through the ward; it is impassable to everyone else.
A permitted traveller appears at the bottom of the stairs in area 14.
On arrival, 1d6 days have passed in the mortal world.
fields.title: Pass Through the Ghostly Candle Ward
fields.trigger: A character attempts to enter one of the forest paths through the floating candles.

steps: Treat the forest as hazardous fairy woodland.
Introduce a possible encounter with giant spiders, frost elves, or winter wolves.
fields.title: Wander in the Hoar-Clad Forest
fields.trigger: Characters leave the safer glade and wander in the treacherous fairy woods.

steps: Griddlegrim checks the visitor’s name.
Invited wedding guests are admitted.
An uninvited person may enter by eating one mushroom from Griddlegrim’s Pouch of Limitless Fungi and resolving its magic.
fields.title: Gain Entry to the Wedding
fields.trigger: A visitor asks Griddlegrim to enter the tower.

steps: The cooks shout orders at the characters.
They demand that the characters carry additional food upstairs to the wedding feast.
fields.title: Help the Frost Elf Cooks
fields.trigger: The characters enter the Fairy Kitchen and the cooks notice them.

steps: The pantry appears larger the farther one explores it.
For each person and each turn spent searching, roll a 1-in-6 chance of finding treasure worth 2d10 × 10 gp in the mortal world.
Possible finds include rare fairy wines, jellied dreams, sprite dust, and tarts of infatuation.
fields.title: Raid the Fairy Pantry
fields.trigger: A character spends time searching deeper into the pantry.

steps: The mortal makes a save versus spells.
On a failed save, the mortal forever yearns to return to Fairy.
fields.title: Eat or Drink at the Fairy Feast
fields.trigger: A mortal consumes food or drink from the wedding feast.

steps: The guards move immediately to intervene.
They escort the uninvited visitors to Princess Snowfall-at-Dusk in area 19.
fields.title: Escort Uninvited Guests to the Princess
fields.trigger: The four frost elf guards identify uninvited visitors at the wedding feast.

steps: Either slay the ghost, or undo the soul-binding on the ring.
Unbinding may be achieved through one of the ring’s stated release conditions.
fields.title: End Sir Chyde’s Haunting
fields.trigger: The possessor of the stolen Ring of Soul-Binding is being haunted by Sir Chyde’s ghost.

steps: Return through the warded route to Sir Chyde’s tomb.
Take the ring from Sir Chyde’s coffer.
Bring the ring into Fairy; Sir Chyde’s soul follows it, allowing the lovers to reunite and marry.
The princess may reward the characters with jewels or by granting one wish.
fields.title: Fulfil the Princess’s Plea
fields.trigger: Princess Snowfall-at-Dusk asks the characters to reunite her with Sir Chyde.

fields.title: Entrance Hall Admission Check
fields.trigger: Visitors arrive at the tower door and Griddlegrim checks their names against the wedding guests.

fields.title: Frost Elf Nobles Disturbed
fields.trigger: The subdued nobles at the feast are disrupted or bothered; they respond ambivalently and summon the guards.

fields.title: The Lovers Reunited
fields.trigger: The Ring of Soul-Binding is carried from Sir Chyde’s tomb into Fairy. The mortal and fairy regions then begin to separate; within a day or two, the passages between areas 14 and 15 vanish and area 14 again becomes a vaulted chamber with a pool.

fields.title: The Ring Stolen
fields.trigger: Someone removes the Ring of Soul-Binding from the tomb and keeps it. Sir Chyde’s ghost visits the possessor nightly, first pleading for the ring’s return and promising his fairy bride’s generosity, then becoming angry and violent if refused.

fields.title: Fairy Prison Random Event Check
fields.trigger: Every two turns in the Fairy Prison, there is a 1-in-6 chance that one event from the Random Events table occurs.

entries.result: 1d3 frost elf knights, guests of the princess, emerge from the forest on white chargers.
A cawing white raven brings the princess a message announcing the arrival of her friend, Lord Mantle-of-Runes.
A laden sleigh pulled by white stags rushes from the forest. Its goblin rider brings fairy fruits, ice wines, and a cauldron of steaming soup to the tower.
2d6 dire wolves creep from the forest and sniff around the lake, seeking prey.

fields.title: Random Events (1-in-6 Chance Every Two Turns)

entries.result: Double in size, destroying clothing. Double melee damage. Lasts 1d6 turns.
Shrink to 6” tall for 1d6 turns.
Skin turns permanently purple.
Eyes shrivel up. New eyes grow on palms of hands, 1 turn later.
All hair on body grows to 10’ long.
Nose swells, grows a sour face, and becomes sentient. It is endlessly critical of the PC’s actions.
+1 to a random ability score.
Eyes enlarge and emit yellow light in a 30’ radius.
Warm, fuzzy feeling. Automatically make next saving throw.
Body turns transparent for 1d6 turns. Can surprise on a 1–4, if naked.
Alternate weeping and hysterical laughter when spoken to. Lasts 1d6 turns.
Vomit up a stream of worms and maggots. Unable to do anything else for 1d6 turns.

fields.role: Three lurking predators that guard the rough passage beneath the mound.
fields.title: Wormtongues in the worm hole

fields.role: Animated guardians of area 5 that attack characters who are not Lawful.
fields.title: Floating religious objects

fields.role: Two dancing skeletons that welcome strangers into the family crypt and invite them to join.
fields.title: Floating skeleton dancers

fields.role: Three lurking predators in the hole at area 10.
fields.title: Wormtongues in the priest’s quarters

fields.role: Two guardians of the double doors in area 12.
fields.title: Stone hounds

fields.role: A ghost in the knight’s tomb who beseeches the player characters to help him.
fields.title: Sir Chyde

fields.role: Goblin doorman at the tower entrance, riding on Grimmlegridge and carrying a pouch of mushrooms that can be offered to unlisted visitors.
fields.title: Griddlegrim

fields.role: A troll who carries the goblin doorman Griddlegrim on his back in the entrance hall.
fields.title: Grimmlegridge

fields.role: Two cooks bustling around the fairy kitchen and baking.
fields.title: Frost elf cooks

fields.role: Five frost elf knights seated at the feast in area 18.
fields.title: Frost elf knights at the wedding feast

fields.role: Seven frost elf nobles seated at the feast in area 18.
fields.title: Frost elf nobles at the wedding feast

fields.role: Four guards positioned at the edges of the wedding feast room.
fields.title: Wedding feast guards

fields.role: The princess in area 19, eager to speak with strangers and especially interested in mortals.
fields.title: Princess Snowfall-at-Dusk

fields.text: The dusty floor in area 5 conceals a mosaic.
fields.title: Concealed floor mosaic

fields.text: The double doors in area 5 are inscribed “The Most Dear”.
fields.title: Hall of guardians door inscription

fields.text: A tapestry in the Chapel of St Sedge conceals the west door.
fields.title: Concealed west door in the chapel

fields.text: A hidden flagstone is located in the northeast corner of area 10.
fields.title: Hidden flagstone in the priest’s quarters

fields.text: A mural in area 11 is partially concealed on the mould-patched walls.
fields.title: Partially concealed mural

fields.text: The double doors are inscribed “Call to the companions”. The password that prevents the stone hounds from attacking is “Flaegr and Chedr”.
fields.title: Hall of hounds inscription and password

fields.description: A tangled forest approach. Clanking metal can be heard from area 2.
fields.title: 1. Approaching the mound

fields.description: Rune-etched stones stand among branches hung with clanking iron owls. A twitching stag skeleton is coated in bright green slime that is evaporating.
fields.title: 2. The Whything Stones

fields.description: A heavy granite slab, overgrown with lichen and wild roses, seals stairs that descend into the dank, silent dark of the tomb at area 5.
fields.title: 3. Tomb entrance

fields.description: A rough, 2-foot-wide hole burrows into the earth beneath the mound. Three wormtongues lurk inside. Acidic slime trails run from the hole into the woods, and the passage descends to area 10.
fields.title: 4. Worm hole

fields.description: A musty, wet hall. Floating religious objects attack non-Lawful characters. Dust on the floor conceals a mosaic. Double doors bear the inscription “The Most Dear”.
fields.title: 5. Hall of guardians

fields.description: A statue of Princess Snowfall-at-Dusk is blindfolded and posed with one finger at her lips.
fields.title: 6. Blindfolded statue

fields.description: A mirror that can freeze characters who pass in front of it.
fields.title: 7. Freezing mirror

fields.description: Two floating skeletons dance in the crypt and welcome strangers to join them. Sheets of slime drip from the ceiling into a fissure that descends to area 15.
fields.title: 8. Family crypt

fields.description: A chapel with decaying pews and a stone altar bearing a candle. A tapestry conceals the west door.
fields.title: 9. Chapel of St Sedge

fields.description: Three wormtongues lurk in a hole and attack when disturbed by noise. The room contains rubble from a collapsed wall and a mouldy writing desk. A flagstone is hidden in the northeast corner.
fields.title: 10. Abandoned priest’s quarters

fields.description: Weapon-bearing statues stand among mould-patched walls. A mural is partially concealed.
fields.title: 11. Statues with weapons

fields.description: A hall with carved pillars and double doors inscribed “Call to the companions”. Two stone hounds attack if the door is touched without first speaking the password “Flaegr and Chedr”.
fields.title: 12. Hall of hounds

fields.description: The ghost of Sir Chyde asks the player characters for help. The tomb contains a stone coffer, a portrait of Princess Snowfall-at-Dusk, and tarnished silver candlesticks.
fields.title: 13. The knight’s tomb

fields.description: Ghostly, floating votive candles wait at the bottom of the stairs. Passing through them transports characters to Fairy at area 15.
fields.title: 14. Warded pool

fields.description: A snow-clad glade lies in an ominous fir wood. A white marble tower with 3 floors stands in the middle of a frozen lake beneath a purple fissure in the sky. Ghostly floating votive candles ward the forest paths; passing through them transports eligible characters to the tomb at area 14.
fields.title: 15. Tower on a frozen lake

fields.description: Griddlegrim, a goblin doorman, rides on the back of the troll Grimmlegridge. The hall smells of cooking from area 17 and is decorated with garlands and rows of cosy boots and coats. Visitors not on the guest list may be admitted if they eat a mushroom from Griddlegrim’s pouch.
fields.title: 16. Entrance hall

fields.description: Two frost elf cooks bustle around baking. The pantry is stuffed with fairy delicacies.
fields.title: 17. Fairy kitchen

fields.description: Five frost elf knights and 7 frost elf nobles sit at a feast. A table is covered with luxurious provender, 4 guards stand at the room’s edges, and the atmosphere is subdued.
fields.title: 18. Wedding feast

fields.description: Princess Snowfall-at-Dusk is here and is excited to talk with strangers, especially mortals. A canopy bed is veiled in snow dust, and jewellery boxes sit on the dressing table.
fields.title: 19. The princess’s bedchamber

Statistics: AC 3 [16], HD 5* (26 hp), Att 1 × touch (1d6 + aging), THAC0 15 [+4], MV 60’ (20’), SV D10 W11 P12 B13 S14 (5), ML 11, AL Lawful, XP 300. accepted_uncertainties.rationale: Source states directly, "(The referee may decide how accurate this genealogical information is.)" (p8). The ambiguity is authorial, not an extraction error, so the record's uncertainty is accepted as-is.
Source frames human sacrifice explicitly as "rumours" feared common folk repeat about the Drune (p12), not a confirmed fact about the Drune themselves. The record correctly preserves this as rumor.

The betrothal account sits under the page's own "Common Folklore" heading, introduced as a tale "known among the common folk of Dolmenwood, and may be heard by PCs" (p9), explicitly distinguished from the "Deeper Investigation" section's confirmed facts. Treating it as unverified folklore matches the source's own framing.

Under "Common Folklore" (p9), the Lady's fate is hedged with "Some say she died..." and is directly contradicted by the confirmed referee background elsewhere (p19, p31) that the princess remains imprisoned in Fairy. The source itself sets up folklore vs. confirmed truth as separate, intentionally conflicting layers.
This entry is under the "Common Folklore" heading (p9), introduced as common-folk hearsay rather than referee-confirmed history, matching how the source itself frames the section.

Source states the runes, "if deciphered, appears to have some function in rituals of summoning" (p12) -- a deliberately approximate identification, not a full mechanical rule. No further detail on the runes' function is given anywhere in the evidence pack.

Source states referees "may locate this adventure in any hex outside of the Witching Ring, Chell" and that "the events of the adventure do not relate to any specific location within the forest" (p5) -- the vagueness is an intentional design choice, not a missed detail.

The "Outside the Mound" table (p11) gives a 1-in-6 chance every two turns for a random event, and lists four numbered entries, but never states the die or method (e.g. d4) used to choose among them once triggered. No other page in the pack supplies this rule.
Source states directly, "(The referee may decide how accurate this genealogical information is.)" (p8), so the genealogy's accuracy is intentionally left open by the text.
Source states the reward is "5,000gp (or whatever the referee wishes)" (p8), explicitly offering the amount as a default subject to referee substitution.

The yearly weakening of the Cold Prince's banishment appears under the page's "Common Folklore" heading (p9) among common-folk hearsay, not in a section the source marks as referee-confirmed background.
Source states the relative "bequeath[s] some minor wealth to the PC (whatever the referee wishes)" (p8), leaving amount and form to the table.

Source describes the longsword's glamour as compelling wielders "to attack the largest foe in battle" (p18) without stating a saving throw against the effect or a tie-breaking method when multiple foes are equally large; no other page in the pack supplies these rules.

Source lists remedies for the frozen condition (holy water, cure light wounds, sunlight) and separately notes the mirror's own magic fades after a month if removed (p15), but never states how long the frozen condition itself lasts if no remedy is applied.

Source explicitly defers the daily haunting's detailed effects to "see Epilogue, p23" (p19), which lies outside this evidence pack's cited pages, so the effect cannot be further specified from the cited source.

The Burial Mound random-event table (p14) gives a 1-in-6 chance every two turns and four numbered entries, but does not state the die or method used to choose among them, matching the same unspecified-selection gap as the Outside the Mound table on p11.
Source states a visitor not on the guest list "may be allowed entry" after eating the mushroom (p31) -- explicitly non-guaranteed -- and states no other effect the mushroom has on the eater.

The map key text for area 7 on p29 repeats the paralysis trigger but states no duration or end condition for the frozen state, consistent with the same gap confirmed against the full room description on p15.

Reviewed page-0029.png: the lower-level inset shows area 14 with two unlabeled exit arrows, and the main map only states "stairs down to area 14" separately for areas 6 and 7 (p15) without cross-referencing which inset arrow serves which room. The pairing cannot be determined from the cited source.
Same as the area-6 stair pairing: page-0029.png's lower-level inset gives two unlabeled arrows out of area 14, and the source never states which one is reached from area 7.

Page 30 states passing through the tower's wards returns characters to area 14, and that those who did not originate from the tomb cannot pass the wards, but neither p29 nor p30 states or shows any route traveling back through the purple sky fissure from area 15 to area 8.
Source states entry after eating the mushroom is something a visitor "may be allowed" (p31), an explicitly conditional outcome rather than a guaranteed passage.

uncertainties.description: The claimed family connection to the PC may be inaccurate at the referee's discretion.
Human sacrifice is presented as rumor among common folk, not as confirmed fact.
The account intentionally omits the Lady's true identity and simplifies the exchange of rings.
The Lady's supposed death is an unverified rumor and contradicts the referee background that she remains imprisoned.
This record preserves the setting's common folklore and is not wholly equivalent to referee-confirmed history.
The exact function of the runes is not stated; deciphering only indicates an apparent connection to summoning rituals.
The source deliberately leaves the adventure's exact Dolmenwood hex unspecified.
The page numbers four events but does not explicitly state the die used to select among them.
The referee decides whether the supplied genealogy is accurate.
The referee may replace the stated 5,000 gp reward with another amount.
The yearly weakening of the banishment is presented as common folklore rather than confirmed referee background.
The amount and form of the minor inherited wealth are left to the referee.
The source does not specify a saving throw against the longsword's glamour or how to resolve ties for the largest foe.
The source does not specify the natural duration of the frozen condition if none of the listed remedies is used.
The detailed effects of the daily haunting are deferred to the Epilogue on p23, outside this evidence pack.
The source numbers four results but does not state which die or selection method chooses among them after an event is triggered.
The wording says the visitor may be allowed entry; it does not state that eating the mushroom guarantees admission or what other effect the mushroom has.
The page does not state the duration of the frozen condition or how it ends.
The main map and lower-level inset show paired stairs, but do not explicitly label which lower-level stair corresponds to the stair reached from area 6.
The main map and lower-level inset show paired stairs, but do not explicitly label which lower-level stair corresponds to the stair reached from area 7.
No return route from area 15 through the purple sky fissure is shown or stated.
